# Quantum Permutation Noise Limits — scientific navigation

Scientific question: quantum communication through n qubits after an unrecorded uniform permutation and independent local noise. Distinguish coherent quantum capacity from zero-error classical message counts. Rates are per complete block, not per physical qubit.

Start: README.md and science/README.md.

Authoritative scientific routes:
- Model, exact resource and channel assumptions: science/model.md
- All-spin-sector Schur–Weyl and singlet-padding channel identity, including references: science/schur_reduction.md
- Symmetric partial trace, Choi spectrum, EB CP comparator and covariant simulation: science/symmetric_loss.md
- Exact two-way and unassisted flagged-erasure capacity proofs: science/erasure_capacities.md
- Replacer-containing local noise, CP order, adaptive strong-converse fidelity: science/replacement_noise.md
- Constructive classical-message growth and output-dimension upper bound: science/classical_contrast.md
- Physical story, crossover and scope: science/interpretation.md
- Finite real-deformation physical projection, exact conditional loss, strict two-spin achievable-rate improvement, all-sector entropy ceiling, positive lower bound and finite-time limitation: science/finite_deformation_erasure.md

Sister relationship:
- Quantum-Group-Memory-Laws: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Group-Memory-Laws
- The sister owns the full first-mismatch/posterior theorem at science/first_mismatch.md and direct full-channel capacity consequence at science/capacity.md; the versioned links are in science/finite_deformation_erasure.md.
- This repository owns the ordinary Schur/symmetric-loss benchmark and operational comparison. This is one shared deformed all-sector result with two complementary accounts.

Source and evidence routes:

Critical distinctions:
- Full physical twirl acts on the transmitted register, not jointly on the reference.
- Symmetric inputs are optimal for the erasure benchmark, but the converse covers arbitrary encoders.
- f_n(q) is the exact two-way capacity of flagged erasure and an upper bound for replacer-containing noise.
- log2 K_n(q) gives a strong-converse fidelity threshold, not necessarily the true capacity.
- The exact unassisted formula is for flagged erasure; the depolarizing capacity is not determined.
- Fixed positive q and q scaling like c/n have different limits.
- Symmetric loss/resource identities and sector simulation are credited to existing work.
- The deformed chapter uses r for deformation and p for erasure; ordinary chapters retain q for noise probability.
- Equal conserved-algebra dimensions or a global algebra isomorphism do not equate physical local-erasure channels.
- The finite-r theorem bounds arbitrary encoders and adaptive two-way communication; local autocorrelation is not a capacity proxy.
- The deformed exact capacity and sharp ceiling remain undetermined; a finite-time realization requires a separate mixing-time/error account.
- Personal coaching instructions and learner records do not belong in this repository.
